In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿By the fig and the olive﴾ ﴿and Mount Sinin﴾ ﴿and this secure city﴾

Know that the difficulty is that the fig and the olive are not among noble things, so how is it fitting for Allah the Exalted to swear by them? Because of this question, two opinions arose concerning it.

The first: the intended meaning of "the fig and the olive" is these two well-known things. Ibn 'Abbas said: "It is your fig and your olive, this one." Then they mentioned some of the special properties of the fig and the olive.

As for the fig, they said: it is food, fruit, and medicine. As for its being food, physicians claimed that it is a light food, quick to digest, that does not remain in the stomach. It softens the temperament, expels perspiration, reduces phlegm, purifies the two kidneys, removes the sand in the bladder, fattens the body, opens the pores of the liver and spleen, and it is the best and most praiseworthy of fruits. It is related that "a tray of figs was presented to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he ate from it, then said to his companions: 'Eat. If I were to say that a fruit had descended from Paradise, I would say it is this, for the fruit of Paradise is without pits. So eat it, for it cuts off hemorrhoids and benefits gout.'" And from 'Ali ibn Musa al-Rida, peace be upon them both: "The fig removes bad breath, lengthens the hair, and is a safeguard against paralysis." As for its being medicine, it is because it is used as a remedy for expelling the excess matter of the body.

Know that, beyond what we have mentioned, it has properties:

One: its outside is like its inside. It is not like the walnut, whose outside is a shell, nor like the date, whose inside is a shell. Rather, we say that among fruits there are those whose outside is bad and whose inside is good, like the walnut and the watermelon, and among them are those whose outside is good but whose inside is not, like the date and the plum. As for the fig, it is good on the outside and on the inside.

Two: trees are of three kinds. A tree that promises and breaks its promise, which is the tree of disagreement; a second that promises and fulfills, which is the one that brings forth blossom first and after it fruit, like the apple and others; and a tree that gives before the promise, which is the fig, because it produces its fruit before it promises blossom. Indeed, if you changed the expression, you would say: it is a tree that shows the meaning before the claim. Indeed, you may say: it is a tree that produces its fruit before it clothes itself in blossom or leaves. The apple, the apricot, and others begin with themselves and then with others, whereas the fig tree concerns itself with others before concerning itself with itself. Thus all other trees are like the men of business in his saying, peace be upon him: "Begin with yourself, then with those you support." The fig tree is like the Chosen One, peace be upon him, who would begin with others, and if anything remained he would turn it to himself. Indeed, it is among those whom Allah praised in His saying: ﴿They prefer them over themselves, though they themselves are in need﴾ [al-Hashr: 9].

Three: among the special properties of this tree is that when other trees drop their fruit from its place, it does not return in that year, except the fig, which regenerates its seed, and perhaps it falls and then returns a second time.

Four: the fig in a dream is a good and wealthy man; whoever obtains it in a dream obtains wealth and abundance, and whoever eats it, Allah grants him children.

Five: it is related that when Adam, peace be upon him, disobeyed and his garments left him, he covered himself with fig leaves. It is also related that when he descended, wearing fig leaves as a loincloth, he felt lonely, so the gazelles came around him, and he became at ease with them and fed them some fig leaves. Allah granted them beauty in form and grace in meaning, and changed their blood to musk. When the gazelles dispersed to their dwellings, he saw other gazelles with the beauty that pleased him. The next day the gazelles came to Adam following the first ones, and he fed them some of the leaves, so Allah changed their condition to beauty without musk. That is because the first came to Adam not out of greed, while the other group came out of greed, secretly, and to Adam openly. So He changed the outward and not the inward.

As for the olive, its tree is the blessed tree: it is fruit in one respect, condiment in another, and medicine in another. In most lands it does not need the care of people. Moreover, its benefit is not limited to nourishing your body; it is also fuel for the lamp. Its growth in mountains where there is no oiliness at all. It has been said: whoever takes olive leaves in a dream holds fast to the firm handhold. A patient said to Ibn Sirin: "I saw in a dream as if it were said to me: 'Eat the two greens and you will be healed.'" He said: "Eat the olive, for it is neither eastern nor western." Then the commentators said: the fig and the olive are names for these two foodstuffs, and in them are these great benefits, so it is obligatory to apply the word to its apparent meaning, and to be certain that Allah the Exalted swore by them because of these benefits and advantages.

The second opinion: the intended meaning is not these two fruits. They mentioned several views:

One: Ibn 'Abbas said: they are two mountains of the Holy Land, called in Syriac Tur Tina and Tur Zita, because they are the places where the fig and the olive grow. So it is as if He the Exalted swore by the places where the prophets arose. The mountain associated with the fig belongs to 'Isa, peace be upon him. The olive is al-Sham, the place of the mission of most of the prophets of the Children of Israel, and the Tur is the place of the mission of Musa, peace be upon him, and the Secure City is the place of the mission of Muhammad (ﷺ). So the real purpose of the oath is to glorify the prophets and to exalt their ranks.

Two: the intended meaning of the fig and the olive is two mosques. Ibn Zayd then said: the fig is the Mosque of Damascus and the olive is the Mosque of Bayt al-Maqdis. Others said: the fig is the mosque of the Companions of the Cave, and the olive is the mosque of Iliya. And from Ibn 'Abbas: the fig is the Mosque of Noah built on al-Judi, and the olive is the Mosque of Bayt al-Maqdis. Those who hold this view went to it because swearing by a mosque is more excellent, since it is a place of worship and obedience. Since these mosques are in places where fig and olive abound, He therefore suffices with mentioning the fig and the olive.

Three: the intended meaning of the fig and the olive is two lands. Ka'b said: the fig is Damascus and the olive is Bayt al-Maqdis. Shahr ibn Hawshab said: the fig is Kufa and the olive is al-Sham. From al-Rabi': they are two mountains between Hamadan and Hulwan. Those who hold this view went to it because the Jews, the Christians, the Muslims, and the polytheists of Quraysh each glorify one of these lands,

[Page 11]
so Allah the Exalted swore by all these lands together. Or it may be said: Damascus and Bayt al-Maqdis contain the blessings of this world, while the Tur and Mecca contain the blessings of religion.

As for His saying the Exalted: ﴿and Mount Sinin﴾, the intended meaning of "al-Tur" is the mountain on which Allah the Exalted spoke to Musa, peace be upon him. The scholars differed concerning ﴿Sinin﴾. According to the grammarians, the preferred view is that Sinin and Sina are two names for the place in which the mountain is located, and they were attached to that place. As for the commentators, Ibn 'Abbas said, in a narration from 'Ikrimah: "al-Tur" is the mountain, and "Sinin" means "the beautiful" in the language of Abyssinia. Mujahid said: ﴿Sinin﴾ means "the blessed." al-Kalbi said: it is the mountain covered with trees, possessing trees. Muqatil said: every mountain in which there are fruit-bearing trees is Sinin and Sina in the language of the Nabataeans. Al-Wahidi said: the preferred view is that Sinin is the name of the place where the mountain is, and then the mountain was named Sinin or Sina because of its beauty or because it is blessed. It is not permissible for Sinin to be an adjective of al-Tur, because it is in an idafa construction with it.

As for His saying the Exalted: ﴿and this secure city﴾, the intended meaning is Mecca. "al-Amin" means "the safe." The author of al-Kashshaf said: from amina al-rajul amanatan, so he is amin, and his trustworthiness is that he protects whoever enters it as a trustworthy person protects what is entrusted to him. It is also permissible for it to be fa'il in the sense of maf'ul, from amina-hu, because it is one whose dangers are secured, just as it is described as safe in His saying: ﴿a sanctuary secure﴾ [al-Qasas: 57], meaning possessing security. They mentioned several views concerning its being secure:

One: Allah the Exalted protected it from the Elephant, as its explanation will come to you, Allah willing.

Two: it protects for you all things, so one whose blood is permitted, upon resorting to it, is safe from beasts of prey, and game animals gain protection from it upon resorting to it.

Three: it is related that 'Umar used to kiss the Black Stone and say: "You are a stone that neither harms nor benefits. Had I not seen the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) kissing you, I would not have kissed you." 'Ali, peace be upon him, said to him: "Indeed it does harm and benefit. When Allah the Exalted took the covenant from the descendants of Adam, He wrote it on a white parchment, and this corner on that day had a tongue, two lips, and two eyes. He said: 'Open your mouth,' and He made it swallow that parchment, and said: 'Bear witness for whoever meets you, by meeting you, on the Day of Resurrection.'" 'Umar said: "I will not remain among a people in whose midst you are not, O Abu al-Hasan."

The scholars have mentioned several aspects of explaining this excellence.

The first: Allah created every living creature bent over toward its face, except man, for Allah created him tall of stature, taking his food with his hand. Al-Asamm said: it means in the most perfect intellect, understanding, manners, knowledge and eloquence. The summary is that the first view refers to the outward form, and the second to the inward character. It is also reported from Yahya ibn Aktham al-Qadi that he interpreted "taqwim" as beauty of form. He related that a king of his time was alone with his wife on a moonlit night, and said: "If you are not more beautiful than the moon, then you are such-and-such (divorced)." All the jurists issued a ruling that the oath was broken, except Yahya ibn Aktham, who said: "It is not broken." It was said to him: "You have opposed your teachers." He said: "The fatwa is by knowledge, and one more knowing than us has issued a fatwa, namely Allah, exalted is He, for He says: ﴿Indeed, We created man in the best of stature.﴾" And some of the righteous used to say: "O our God, You gave us the best of forms in this world, so give us the best of deeds in the Hereafter, which is pardon for sins and overlooking of faults."

Regarding the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾, there are two opinions.

The first: Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with him) said: it means the most abject age (ardhal al-ʿumr), and it is like His saying: "He is brought back to the most abject age." Ibn Qutaybah said: "The lowest ones (al-sāfilūn) are the weak, the chronically disabled, and those who are unable to devise a plan and find no way." It is said: safala yasfulu, so he is sāfil (low), and they are sāfilūn, just as it is said: ʿalā yaʿlū, so he is ʿāl (high), and they are ʿālūn. He meant that the decrepit man becomes senile, his hearing and sight and intellect weaken, his resourcefulness diminishes, and he becomes unable to do righteous deeds, so he becomes the lowest of all. Al-Farrāʾ said: "If it had been asfala sāfil, it would have been correct, because the word insān (human) is singular, and you say: 'This is the best standing man' (afḍal qāʾim), and you do not say 'best standing men' (afḍal qāʾimīn). However, it was said sāfilīn in the plural because insān has the sense of a plural. It is like His saying: ﴿And he who brings the truth and confirms it—those are the righteous﴾ [al-Zumar: 33], and His saying: ﴿And when We let man taste mercy from Us, he rejoices in it, but if an affliction touches them﴾ [al-Shūrā: 48]."

The second opinion: what Mujāhid and al-Ḥasan mentioned, "Then We return him to the Fire." ʿAlī, peace be upon him, said: "He placed the gates of Hell one below another, so he begins with the lowest and fills it, and it is the lowest of the low." According to this interpretation, the meaning is: "Then We return him to the lowest of the low, to the Fire."

As for the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, know that this exception, according to the first opinion, is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ, an exception not of the same category as what precedes it), and the meaning is: "But those who were righteous among the aged will have an everlasting reward for their obedience and their patience with Allah's trial of them through old age and decrepitude, and for enduring hardships, performing worship, and persevering despite their weakness." As for the second opinion, the exception is connected (muttaṣil, of the same category), and its connection is clear.

As for the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿So for them is an unfailing reward﴾, there are two opinions:

One: not diminished and not cut off.

The second: an unfailing reward, meaning one that is not bestowed with reproach, that is, He does not reproach them for it. Know that all of these are attributes of reward, because it must be uninterrupted and must not be spoiled by reproach.

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Is not Allah the most just of judges?﴾ Concerning it there are two issues:

The first issue: They have mentioned two interpretations of it.

One of them: that this is a confirmation of what was mentioned about the creation of man and then his being returned to the lowest state of old age. Allah, exalted is He, says: Is not the One who did that the most just of judges in His craftsmanship and governance? When power and wisdom are established by this evidence, it is correct to affirm the possibility of the Resurrection (ḥashr) and its occurrence. As for its possibility, it is by considering power; as for its occurrence, it is by considering wisdom, because its absence would impugn wisdom, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in vain. That is the assumption of those who disbelieve﴾ [Ṣād 38:27].

The second: that this is a reminder from Allah, exalted is He, to His Prophet, peace be upon him, that He will judge between him and his opponents on the Day of Resurrection with justice.

The second issue: The judge (al-Qāḍī, i.e. ʿAbd al-Jabbār) said: This verse is among the strongest proofs that He, exalted is He, does not do what is ugly (qabīḥ) and does not create the actions of His servants, given the folly and injustice that are in them. For if the doer of the actions of the servants were Allah, exalted is He, then every folly, every command to folly, and every encouragement to folly would be from Allah, exalted is He, and whoever is like that is the most foolish of fools. Just as there is no wisdom, no command to wisdom, and no encouragement to wisdom except from Allah, exalted is He, and whoever is like that is the most wise of the wise. Since both attributes are established with respect to Allah, exalted is He, describing Him as the most wise of the wise is no more fitting than describing Him as the most foolish of fools. And since this description is impossible with respect to Allah, exalted is He, we know that He is not the creator of the actions of the servants. The answer: the counter-argument is with knowledge and motive. Then we say: the foolish one is the one in whom folly subsists, not the one who created folly, just as the moving and the still are the ones in whom motion and stillness subsist, not the one who created them. And Allah, glorified and exalted is He, knows best what is correct, and may Allah bless our master Muhammad, and his family and companions, and grant them peace.
